summary: Dedicated pool IO wave causing gradual p99 latency regression and transient GPU allocation failures
description:
Issue summary:
Customer (Acme Retail) reports steady degradation of tail latency (p95->p99) across their reserved dedicated pool over the last 18 hours with intermittent failures to allocate GPU slots for batched requests. The impact has been progressively worsening during US-West peak hours, causing production user-facing timeouts and increased error rates on chat endpoints.

Impact:
- Customers experienced p99 increases from ~350ms to 1.2s on rw-chat-13b-v1 flows.
- Intermittent 5xx errors and 'AllocationFailed' errors for short-lived batched streams.
- Affects 3 critical routes used by Acme's checkout assistant.

Observed timeframe:
- First symptoms observed 2026-03-13 09:50 PDT, escalated after sustained drift through the afternoon.

Environment:
- prod - us-west, Dedicated pool ID: dp-64a1
- Customer tier: dedicated (reserved capacity)
- Affected models: rw-decoder-3b-v2 (tokenization-heavy), rw-chat-13b-v1 (longer contexts)

Steps to reproduce (customer):
1) Send high-concurrency chat requests to /v1/chat/stream with message sizes ~1.5k tokens per conversation.
2) Observe p99 latency on the route and occasional allocation failures reported in client logs.
3) Retry shows successful allocation after ~20-60s.

Telemetry & logs (high level):
- Per-route SLO dashboard: steady p95 stable, p99 drift starting 09:50 PDT and spiking during 12:00-16:00 PDT window.
- Serving runtime logs: periodic nvlink and PCIe IO wait warnings on pool nodes (node ids: n-west-023..028).
- Autoscaler: small scale-ups triggered but cluster reported transient GPU attach errors (AttachTimeout) ~10-30s.
- Kernel level: host dmesg on n-west-025 shows repeated NVME queue full / io-wait traces during high load bursts.
- Rate of small short-lived streams (<=5s) from other tenants increased ~3x in same pool during window.

Recent platform changes:
- Rolling OS security update applied to the dedicated pool (dp-64a1) on 2026-03-12 02:00 UTC (non-kernel, I/O subsystem patches).
- Predictive autoscaler tuning change merged last week (PR infra#2314) that alters slot packing thresholds for bursty small streams.

Investigation notes so far:
- Hypothesis A (noisy-neighbor IO pressure): A surge of many small short streams from another tenant is creating NVMe IO queue pressure, increasing host io-wait and delaying GPU attach / batch formation. This is consistent with host dmesg / iostat spikes and the increase in short-stream rate in telemetry.
- Hypothesis B (autoscaler packing change interaction): New packing thresholds cause more slot fragmentation; with IO stalls the autoscaler retries result in AttachTimeout and temporary allocation failures.
- Hypothesis C (hardware/NVMe degradation): Less likely but cannot be ruled out; one node shows higher io wait and SMART warnings queued for review.

Immediate mitigations executed:
- Moved Acme's routes to a sibling dedicated pool (dp-64b9) as a temporary mitigation at 2026-03-13 18:10 PDT. Initial rollback shows p99 back to ~420ms on dp-64b9.
- Throttled a noisy tenant's short-stream rate via per-tenant ingress limit on pool dp-64a1 (emergency throttle) to reduce IO pressure.
- SRE pinned autoscaler to previous slot-packing config for dp-64a1 to observe effects (rollback of infra#2314 was staged).

Next steps / action items:
- SRE (Priya) to run fio/io stress tests on n-west nodes in maintenance window to reproduce NVMe queue saturation and measure recovery characteristics.
- Infra Eng (Jordan) to review infra#2314 effect matrix and propose immediate partial rollback or tuning for dedicated pools handling mixed small+long streams.
- Storage/Hardware ops to check NVMe SMART for nodes n-west-025/027 and schedule replacement if warranted.
- Support to monitor Acme's traffic on dp-64b9 for 24 hours and collect per-route token-level traces for p99.

Customer-facing note prepared and sent to Acme at 2026-03-13 19:00 PDT explaining temporary pool move and ETA for deeper fix.

Desired resolution criteria:
- p99 restored to under 500ms for Acme routes on stable dedicated pool for 24 hours, and allocation failure rate returns to <0.1% over same period.

References:
- Dashboards: https://dashboards.redwood.dev/d/pools/dp-64a1
- Slack thread: #support (ts: 2026-03-13T18:05Z)
